title: 20 youth agri startups reach FAO bootcamp round in Dhaka
excerpt: The top three teams in the FAO-led contest will get help to incubate and scale their ideas through FAO Bangladesh projects.
content:
Twenty agricultural startups led by young people, picked from nearly 90 applications, presented their ideas at the bootcamp round of a contest run by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) in Dhaka, according to a press release issued on Wednesday, 4 November, The Daily Star reported.

FAO Bangladesh and the World Food Forum Bangladesh Chapter held the bootcamp round of “Innovators’ Brew Season II: Youth Agri Startup Olympiad” at Sheraton Dhaka. Teams presented to a panel of experts from FAO and agritech startups.

What comes next

The bootcamp will choose the top teams to pitch to judges at a High-Level Dialogue Forum later in November. The top three teams will get support to integrate, incubate and scale their ideas through innovation hubs in FAO Bangladesh’s current portfolio, according to the report.

Who said what

Dia Sanou, deputy FAO representative in Bangladesh, urged young innovators to see agriculture as “a dynamic sector offering opportunities beyond traditional farming”. Imanun Nabi Khan, assistant FAO representative, encouraged young people to look across the agricultural value chain and work on food security, nutrition and sustainability.

Why it matters

Youth unemployment and the need for jobs outside the informal sector are rising concerns for donors in Bangladesh. Programmes that link young entrepreneurs to UN-backed incubation can be useful partners for NGOs working on livelihoods, nutrition and agriculture.

What to watch

The date of the High-Level Dialogue Forum and the names of the winning teams.
